source: KDIGO 2024 CKD Guideline + KDIGO 2012 AKI Guideline

recommendations.text: In people with CKD, assess risk factors for CA-AKI before contrast exposure
For CA-AKI Risk Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - check baseline egfr (within 60 minutes) - review risk factors (within 60 minutes) - assess hydration status
During CA-AKI Risk Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: administer contrast without egfr, skip risk assessment.
Metformin must be held before and 48h after iodinated contrast. [REQUIRED: hold_metformin_before_contrast, hold_metformin_48h_post] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO Contrast AKI; ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2024

recommendations.text: Metformin must be held before contrast and for 48h after; contrast-induced AKI impairs metformin clearance causing lactic acidosis. [FORBIDDEN: continue_metformin_during_contrast_study, restart_metformin_before_48h_post_contrast] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO Contrast AKI 2012; ACR Contrast Manual 2023; metformin with contrast-induced AKI causes lactic acidosis

recommendations.text: eGFR <30 is high risk for contrast nephropathy. Pre-hydration mandatory. [REQUIRED: prehydrate_iv_ns, use_lowest_contrast_volume] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO Contrast AKI; Mehran R, JACC 2004

recommendations.text: High-risk patients require prehydration before contrast; high-osmolar contrast agents significantly increase nephrotoxicity. [FORBIDDEN: give_contrast_without_prehydration_high_risk, use_high_osmolar_contrast_in_high_risk] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO Contrast AKI 2012; high-osmolar contrast increases nephrotoxicity risk 2-3x; prehydration reduces risk by 40%

recommendations.text: Gadolinium in severe CKD causes nephrogenic systemic fibrosis. [FORBIDDEN: give_gadolinium_contrast, order_mri_with_gadolinium] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2024; FDA NSF Warning

recommendations.text: Dialysis patients may need post-contrast dialysis scheduling. [REQUIRED: schedule_dialysis_post_contrast] (Severity: MODERATE)
NSAIDs with contrast multiply nephrotoxicity risk. [FORBIDDEN: continue_nsaid_with_contrast] (Severity: HIGH)
CKD patients require prehydration and low-osmolar contrast before any contrast exposure. [FORBIDDEN: give_contrast_without_preparation, skip_prehydration, give_high_osmolar_contrast] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO Contrast AKI 2024; ACR Manual on Contrast Media

recommendations.text: Aminoglycosides synergize nephrotoxicity with contrast agents. [FORBIDDEN: continue_aminoglycoside_with_contrast, give_aminoglycoside] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO Contrast AKI 2012; Lopez-Novoa JM, Kidney Int 2011

recommendations.text: Specific nephrotoxins should be held or monitored around contrast exposure. [REQUIRED: hold_nephrotoxin_before_contrast, monitor_drug_levels] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO Contrast AKI 2012; ACR Manual on Contrast Media 2024

recommendations.text: Concurrent nephrotoxins with contrast create additive renal injury; NSAIDs must be held periprocedurally. [FORBIDDEN: continue_nephrotoxin_during_contrast_exposure, give_nsaid_periprocedural_with_contrast] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO Contrast AKI 2012; concurrent nephrotoxins with contrast create additive renal injury

recommendations.text: Gadolinium contrast in severe CKD (eGFR < 30) causes nephrogenic systemic fibrosis, a debilitating fibrotic condition. [FORBIDDEN: give_gadolinium_in_severe_ckd_for_mri, order_mri_gadolinium_without_nephrology_approval_in_ckd] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO Contrast AKI 2012; ACR 2023; gadolinium in eGFR < 30 causes nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF)

recommendations.text: CKD with diabetes doubles contrast nephropathy risk; isotonic prehydration and low-volume contrast are mandatory. [FORBIDDEN: give_contrast_without_isotonic_prehydration_in_ckd, use_high_volume_contrast_in_ckd_diabetes] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO Contrast AKI 2012; CKD + diabetes doubles contrast nephropathy risk; mandatory low-volume iso-osmolar + prehydration

recommendations.text: In people with CKD G3a-G5, use the lowest possible dose of contrast media and ensure adequate hydration before and after contrast media exposure

For High Risk CA-AKI Prevention, the following actions are mandatory: - consider alternative imaging - nephrology consult - hold nephrotoxic medications - iv hydration pre contrast (within 60 minutes) - use minimum contrast volume - iv hydration post contrast - hold metformin if applicable - monitor scr 48 72h (within 4320 minutes)
During High Risk CA-AKI Prevention, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: use high osmolar contrast.
Converted from unconditional: contrast without hydration is harmful when eGFR <60; pre-hydration reduces CA-AKI incidence by 50% [FORBIDDEN: administer_contrast_without_hydration] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO 2024 CKD Section 4.3.2; pre-hydration mandatory in eGFR <60

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: repeated contrast within 48h in CKD patients (eGFR <60) causes cumulative nephrotoxicity [FORBIDDEN: repeat_contrast_within_48h] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO 2024 CKD Section 4.3.2; repeated contrast within 48h multiplies AKI risk

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: continuing NSAIDs during contrast exposure multiplies nephrotoxicity risk via afferent arteriole vasoconstriction [FORBIDDEN: continue_nsaids] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO 2024 CKD; NSAIDs synergize with contrast nephrotoxicity

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: continuing aminoglycosides with contrast exposure causes synergistic tubular toxicity [FORBIDDEN: continue_aminoglycosides] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO 2024 CKD; aminoglycosides synergize with contrast nephrotoxicity

recommendations.text: Ensure adequate hydration before and after contrast media exposure and use the lowest possible dose of contrast media in CKD G3 patients

For Moderate Risk CA-AKI Prevention, the following actions are mandatory: - iv hydration pre contrast (within 60 minutes) - use minimum contrast volume - iv hydration post contrast - monitor scr 48 72h (within 4320 minutes)
During Moderate Risk CA-AKI Prevention, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: use high osmolar contrast.
Converted from unconditional: contrast without hydration in eGFR 30-59 increases CA-AKI risk; pre-hydration is standard of care [FORBIDDEN: administer_contrast_without_hydration] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO 2024 CKD Section 4.3.2; hydration required in CKD G3

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: repeated contrast within 48h at eGFR 30-59 causes cumulative nephrotoxicity [FORBIDDEN: repeat_contrast_within_48h] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: KDIGO 2024 CKD Section 4.3.2; repeated contrast in CKD G3 multiplies AKI risk

recommendations.text: In people with eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73m², the risk of CA-AKI is low and routine prophylactic measures are not required
For Low Risk - Standard Care, the following actions are mandatory: - document egfr check - standard contrast administration
During Low Risk - Standard Care, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: administer contrast without egfr check.
CA-AKI defined as SCr increase ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours OR ≥1.5x baseline
For Post-Contrast Monitoring, the following actions are mandatory: - check scr at 48h (within 2880 minutes) - assess urine output
During Post-Contrast Monitoring, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge without scr check.
Evaluate and treat reversible causes of AKI; avoid nephrotoxic agents and ensure adequate volume status in patients with CA-AKI
For CA-AKI Management, the following actions are mandatory: - nephrology consult (within 120 minutes) - optimize fluid status - avoid additional nephrotoxins - serial scr monitoring
During CA-AKI Management, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: additional contrast exposure, continue nephrotoxic drugs, discharge without followup.
Confirm stable kidney function before discharge and provide instructions on signs of AKI and when to seek medical attention
For Safe Discharge, the following actions are mandatory: - document stable egfr - provide discharge instructions - schedule followup
During Safe Discharge, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge without egfr confirmation.
